title: Adaptive KV-affinity streaming scheduler tuning for mixed prompt/response workloads
creator: Priya Raman
description: Tuning the continuous/streaming batching scheduler to maintain latency SLOs and reduce GPU memory fragmentation for mixed prompt/response length workloads by introducing KV-affinity placement and adaptive coalescing thresholds.
goals: Reduce p95 inference latency regressions for mixed-length dialogues by >= 15% during peak load
Decrease average KV cache residency footprint per GPU by >= 12% without impacting generation quality
Maintain or improve token throughput for steady-state traffic
Provide config knobs + safe rollout for Dedicated and Hosted deployments
success_metrics: p50 latency delta compared to baseline: target <= +5ms
p95 latency reduction: target >= 15% vs baseline for mixed workloads
GPU memory headroom increase: target >= 12% reduction in average KV occupancy
Unit cost per 1M tokens: <= 5% increase (prefer decrease)
design_summary: Introduce a lightweight KV-affinity heuristic inside the continuous streaming scheduler. When a request arrives, the scheduler records a short fingerprint of the request's prefix length and KV-residency sensitivity. The scheduler preferentially coalesces requests that are likely to share KV residency locality (same model variant, similar prefix length buckets, and compatible KV pin preferences). We add a new coalesce_threshold adaptive function that backs off coalescing when headroom is low and re-aggresses when KV eviction rate is low. The change is purely scheduling-level; model kernels remain unchanged.
algorithm_details:
1) Compute affinity key: (model_id, quantization_profile, prefix_bucket).
2) Maintain per-GPU soft KV-residency counters sampled over 1s windows.
3) On enqueue, candidate joins queue segment for affinity key. Coalescing allowed only within same affinity segment unless headroom >= threshold.
4) Adaptive coalesce_threshold = base * (1 + alpha * eviction_ratio) where eviction_ratio is damped over 5s.
5) Provide override flags: force_coalesce_for_latency, prefer_kv_locality, and max_coalesce_size.
experiments_planned: A/B in Hosted region us-west-2 with 10% traffic split for 48h using mixed dialog synthetic workload (mix-3) — measure p50/p95, kv-occupancy, evictions/sec
Canary on Dedicated pool (alpha) with 1 GPU fleet for 24h, run replay of real traffic from anonymized traces (week window)
Microbenchmarks: single-GPU stress with tail-heavy prompts to observe slot coalescing and KV thrashing behavior
Regression tests: end-to-end smoke with function-calling and streaming enabled to ensure no protocol regressions
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gate default off. 2) Deploy scheduler binary with kv-affinity disabled to all clusters. 3) Enable flag in non-prod, run automated acceptance for 12h. 4) Enable 10% Hosted traffic A/B for 48h. 5) If metrics meet success criteria, increase to 50% over 24h, then to 100% in 24h. 6) Dedicated: coordinate with capacity team to enable per-pool; start with burstable pools. 7) Revert path: set scheduler.enable_kv_affinity=false and drain coalesced queues.
monitoring: Alert: p95 increase > 10% for 15m in Region X
Telemetry: sample coalesce decisions (trace ids), exported to tracing-service
Logs: gate change events and per-GPU residency snapshots every 10s (low-overhead)
